tasks.task: Establish site and mobilise scaffold materials
tasks.scope: Site induction, permit handover, scaffold material delivery to Kiora Lane and courtyard staging areas, site access control setup.
hazards: Trip hazard from scaffold materials and delivery debris on access routes
Vehicle strike — delivery vehicles moving in courtyard and Kiora Lane with pedestrian activity
Uncontrolled access by residents or unauthorised persons to hazardous areas
Collision between delivery vehicles and site infrastructure or parked vehicles
tasks.dominant_hazard: Vehicle strike — delivery vehicles in occupied courtyard and lane with pedestrian activity
controls: Verify site induction certificate (White Card) held by all personnel before entering site.
Confirm permit handover from principal contractor — check scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder and working at heights permit current.
Establish vehicle exclusion zone in courtyard — barricade with traffic cones and signage, restrict to delivery vehicles only during material drop-off windows.
Direct delivery vehicles to nominated staging areas (Kiora Lane and courtyard) — use spotter to guide reversing vehicles, prohibit unattended reversing.
Remove scaffold packaging and delivery debris from access routes and courtyard immediately after unload — clear to nominated skip or storage area.
Barricade scaffold material stacks in staging areas with chain-link fencing or equivalent — post warning signage 'Do not climb — Scaffold materials'.
Brief all site personnel on access routes, vehicle movement times, and restricted zones — hold toolbox talk before first material delivery.
Post site signage at main entrances and resident notice boards — advise residents of restricted access periods, vehicle movement schedule, and emergency contact.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit worker access to scaffold staging areas until: barricading complete and warning signage installed
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start scaffold erection until: scaffold erection permit and handover certificate received from licenced scaffolder
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: unauthorised persons (residents or public) enter barricaded scaffold material staging areas or approach delivery vehicles
🛑 STOP WORK if: delivery vehicle reversing without spotter present or access route not clear of personnel and trip hazards
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold erection permit or working at heights permit unsigned or not sighted before any scaffold assembly begins
admin: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder — retain on site
Obtain current working at heights permit — verify all personnel listed as authorised
Obtain scaffold handover certificate from licenced scaffolder — mandatory before use
Receive and file noise management plan — confirm communicated to occupants
Schedule delivery windows and post at resident boards minimum 48 hours prior
Record site induction attendance — verify White Card held, document in register
Conduct pre-delivery site walk with supervisor — identify hazards, confirm access routes clear
Appoint spotter for all delivery vehicle reversing — brief on hand signals and radio
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement

monitoring.critical_control: Spotter present and actively directing all delivery vehicle reversing
monitoring.frequency: during each delivery and material movement event
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation spotter stationed, hand signals visible, vehicle stopped when spotter signal given

responsibility.SUP: Supervise site setup, verify permits in place, make sure barricading complete before worker access
responsibility.WKR: Comply with site induction, report unauthorised access, stay clear of vehicle movement zones

tasks.task: Erect scaffold to balcony access points
tasks.scope: Erect and brace scaffold over 4m height via Kiora Lane and courtyard to provide safe working platform for balcony remedial works. Scaffold certification and SWL signage required.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — scaffold collapse or structural failure during erection
Fall from height — worker falls during scaffold assembly and bracing over 4m
Dropped objects from scaffold platform and components onto occupied areas below
Inadequate scaffold stability due to uneven ground or unsecured base plates on hard surfaces
Overloading of scaffold platform during material laydown or worker congestion
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker falls or scaffold structural failure during erection over 4m
controls: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder before any component delivery to site.
Check ground conditions in Kiora Lane and courtyard — measure level variance and identify soft spots, mud, or debris.
Lay timber sole plates (min 50mm hardwood) under all base plates on hard surfaces; compact and level soft ground before plate placement.
Secure all base plates to sole plates with chemical anchors or mechanical fasteners rated for uplift and lateral load.
Erect scaffold according to engineer design and load calculations — do not deviate from approved temporary works plan.
Brace scaffold vertically and horizontally at maximum intervals specified in design; do not begin platform laydown until bracing complete.
Install fall arrest anchor points (rated 15 kN minimum) at scaffold head and ledges before workers access the structure.
Verify all connections are tight; check all ledger bolts, standards, and cross-braces with torque wrench before handover.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not erect scaffold until: engineer-approved temporary works plan and load calculations are provided and on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker access until: licenced scaffolder has signed handover certificate and all fall arrest points are installed and tagged.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any base plate is loose, corroded, or not secured to sole plate — do not continue until repair is certified.
🛑 STOP WORK if: visible ground movement, subsidence, or water pooling beneath sole plates — engineer re-assessment required.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker accesses platform without harness attached to certified anchor point or before handover certificate is displayed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm licenced scaffolder name, licence number, and expiry on scaffold erection permit before work starts.
Record handover date, time, and scaffolder signature on site log before any worker uses platform.
Brief all workers on load limits, fall arrest anchor points, and exclusion zone before scaffold use commences.
Conduct daily visual check of scaffold for loose bolts, damaged standards, or shifted base plates; record in site notebook.
tell building occupants of scaffold erection, exclusion zones, and drop hazard zone below platform.
Keep load calculations, temporary works plan, erection permit, and handover certificate on site for inspection.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Fall arrest harness (certified, inspected) — worn during all erection, bracing, and platform assembly work
Lanyard with certified shock absorber (min 2m length, 15 kN anchor) — attached to harness always above platform edge

monitoring.critical_control: Verify base plates are level and secure before erecting first standard; test with hand pressure and torque wrench.
monitoring.frequency: Before erection commences, then after each major bracing section is complete
monitoring.evidence: Handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder; photographic record of base plate installation and torque wrench readings; daily visual inspection log

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.scope: check exposed concrete slab for cracks, spalling, and defects. Clean substrate. Cut and prepare cracks for repair. Apply concrete repair system per Leo and Associates engineer direction. HOLD: Leo and Associates inspection sign-off before membrane application.
hazards: Trip hazard from exposed cracks and spalling on balcony surface during inspection and cleaning
Cut or laceration from sharp concrete edges and spall fragments
Manual handling injury from concrete removal and cleaning debris bagging
Dust inhalation during concrete cleaning and grinding preparation for repair
tasks.dominant_hazard: Dust inhalation during concrete substrate cleaning and grinding in preparation for repair
controls: Wet-clean concrete substrate with water spray or damp cloth before grinding or cutting to suppress airborne dust.
Use portable dust extraction with HEPA filter attached to grinding or cutting equipment during crack preparation.
Wear P2 or P3 respirator fitted and sealed during grinding, cutting, or dry cleaning of concrete substrate.
Barricade cracked and spalling areas with high-visibility tape and caution signs to prevent trip hazard.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when handling sharp concrete edges, spall fragments, or broken concrete pieces.
Bag and remove concrete cleaning debris daily to prevent manual handling injury and dust re-suspension.
Do not apply membrane coating until Leo and Associates engineer has inspected and signed off substrate repair.
Brief all workers on slab surface hazards — cracks, spalling, trip points — before starting inspection work.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane coating until: Leo and Associates engineer has inspected repair and signed written approval.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: dust extraction equipment fails or is not running during active grinding or cutting.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker dust respirator is visibly damaged, seal is broken, or respirator is removed during dust-generating task.
🛑 STOP WORK if: concrete repair product SDS has not been reviewed by all workers before mixing or application.
admin: Obtain and verify Leo and Associates engineer approval letter before work starts — attach to site file.
Confirm scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder; obtain handover certificate before any worker accesses platform.
Verify working at heights permit is signed and current for all elevated tasks on this slab.
Confirm noise management plan is current and distributed to building occupants before grinding or cutting work.
Brief all workers on concrete repair product SDS; record training attendance and date.
Confirm all workers hold White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and current working-at-heights competency verification (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Collect and retain signed Leo and Associates engineer inspection report before membrane application phase.
ppe: P2 or P3 respirator — fitted and sealed, changed as per cartridge manufacturer schedule
eye protection— to protect against dust and spall fragments
High-visibility vest or jacket — for occupant awareness in occupied building
steel-capped footwear— to reduce trip injury on uneven cracked substrate

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Before each grinding or cutting session; continuously during active dust generation.
monitoring.evidence: Visual and audible verification of extraction operation; worker respirator seal check and cartridge date record; photographic record of wet suppression or extraction setup.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Investigate and repair slab substrate
responsibility.WKR: Perform Investigate and repair slab substrate per SWMS

tasks.task: Remove existing waterproofing, screed and tile bed
tasks.scope: Demo and removal of failed membrane, screed, and tile bed from balcony substrates. Silica-producing demolition — dust control, PPE, and waste bagging required. HOLD: retain samples for asbestos and hazmat assessment if building predates 1990 or visual suspect material present.
hazards: Asbestos disturbance and inhalation if building predates 1990 or visual suspect material present — unconfirmed latent condition
Laceration or puncture wound from broken tiles and sharp tile fragments
Manual handling injury from removal of wet or heavy screed and tile bed sections
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of respirable silica dust during screed and tile demolition
controls: Collect all tile fragments and screed debris in sealed bags on-site — do not sweep or blow dust; use damp cloths and vacuum with HEPA filter only

Retain representative samples of waterproofing membrane, screed, and tile bed in labelled bags for asbestos and hazmat testing before removal proceeds — hold samples if building predates 1990 or visual suspect material visible
Wear heavy-duty cut-resistant gloves and eye protection
Segregate waste into sealed bags marked for disposal — do not mix tile, screed, or membrane waste with general construction waste
Brief all workers on tile fragment hazard, RPE fit-check procedure, and the hold requirement for samples before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove screed or tile bed until: representative samples are collected, retained, and asbestos/hazmat testing results received or waiver confirmed in writing
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: RPE cartridges show visible saturation or resistance increases — replace immediately and brief worker on fit
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust suppression spray fails or is not applied continuously — do not resume breaking or chipping until wet method is reinstated

🛑 STOP WORK if: visual suspect material (friable, discoloured, or layered appearance inconsistent with standard screed) is encountered — isolate area and tell supervisor for hazmat assessment before continuing
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain asbestos/hazmat assessment report before removal proceeds — if building predates 1990, assume potential hazard unless certified otherwise
Verify EPA waste tracking documentation is complete for all sealed waste bags before removal from site
Record all sample collection and testing outcomes in site diary with photos of suspect material locations
Confirm noise management plan compliance with occupant notification schedule if impact tools are used
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Respiratory protective equipment (RPE) — P2 minimum, fit-tested, cartridge replaced when resistance noted
Closed-toe boots with puncture-resistant soles for walking on debris and broken tile

monitoring.critical_control: Water mist spray active and visible during all tile and screed breaking — no dry dust visible
monitoring.frequency: continuous during demolition work
monitoring.evidence: spray nozzle open, wet debris observed, RPE cartridge colour change checked before each break, site diary entry recording spray operation start and end times

responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing waterproofing, screed and per SWMS

tasks.scope: Prepare substrate per membrane manufacturer specification. Apply new membrane system (primer, base coat, reinforcement, top coat) to balcony slab. Coverage and curing per product data sheet and Leo and Associates specification.
hazards: Chemical exposure — inhalation of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and solvent vapours from primer, base coat, and top coat products
Chemical skin contact and irritation from membrane materials and primers
Slippery substrate — wet membrane coating creating slip hazard on balcony during application and curing
Heat stress and dehydration during hot weather application under full PPE and confined balcony conditions
Inadequate ventilation if balcony enclosed or sheltered leading to vapour accumulation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Inhalation of volatile organic compounds and solvent vapours from waterproofing membrane system application
controls: Obtain and review current SDS for primer, base coat, and top coat before work starts.
Establish continuous natural cross-ventilation across balcony — open doors and windows upwind and downwind of work area.
Apply primer and coats only when external temperature is below 28°C and relative humidity below 80% — check BOM forecast before 7am daily.
Wear organic vapour cartridge respirator (AS/NZS 1716 P2 minimum) fitted and tested before each application session.
Wear chemical-resistant chemical-resistant gloves (minimum 0.11mm thickness) — change gloves every 2 hours or if torn.
Wear hi-viz shirt or vest— no bare skin contact with wet membrane.
Mix and decant membrane products in a container with a tight-fitting lid — keep lid closed between applications.
Prohibit entry to balcony by residents and non-workers during application and for 24 hours post-application — post 'Wet Membrane — Do Not Enter' signs at all balcony access points.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not open balcony to residents until: final top coat has fully cured per manufacturer data sheet AND balcony has been ventilated continuously for 4 hours minimum.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane if: external temperature exceeds 28°C or relative humidity exceeds 80% — reschedule to next suitable day.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker reports dizziness, nausea, or excessive sweating — rest worker in shade, provide water, and allow vapour headache to clear before resuming.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed drops below 2 knots for more than 15 minutes — vapours will not clear and accumulate on balcony.
🛑 STOP WORK if: resident or child enters balcony exclusion zone during application — resume only after all persons have left and area is re-barricaded.
admin: Confirm SDS training completed by all applicators — record trainer name, date, and worker signature.
Confirm working at heights permit signed by supervisor before starting — display permit at site entrance.
Confirm scaffold handover certificate issued by licenced scaffolder — attach certificate to site induction pack.
Record daily weather conditions (temperature, humidity, wind speed) in site log.
tell building manager 48 hours before start — provide SDS and confirm ventilation strategy.
Place 'Wet Membrane — Do Not Enter' signs on all balcony access doors — photograph sign placement.
Record application start time, product batch numbers, and completion time in site diary.
Conduct post-application ventilation verification — open all adjacent windows and note clearance time in log.
ppe: Organic vapour cartridge respirator (AS/NZS 1716 P2 minimum) — fitted and seal-tested before each use
hi-viz shirt or vest, not exposed skin)

monitoring.critical_control: Respirator fitted and seal-tested; cross-ventilation maintained; temperature and humidity within limits
monitoring.frequency: each shift start and hourly during application
monitoring.evidence: SDS reviewed; weather log completed; respirator fit test recorded; ventilation verified; worker symptom check documented

responsibility.SUP: Supervise membrane application, verify SDS and controls, sign off hold points, monitor weather limits, manage exclusion zone
responsibility.WKR: Perform membrane application per SWMS, wear all PPE, report dizziness or nausea immediately, comply with temperature and humidity limits

tasks.task: Isolate and protect occupied spaces below balconies
tasks.scope: Install netting, sheeting, and temporary barriers to contain dust and debris. Manage access and movement within building during works. Coordinate with residents for water and power shutdown if required.
hazards: Collapse of temporary netting or barriers from impact, wind, or poor installation
Inadequate isolation — debris or contaminated water bypassing barriers into occupied spaces
Trip hazard from temporary barriers and netting fixings within interior areas
Entanglement or laceration hazard from netting and sharp barrier edges
tasks.dominant_hazard: Collapse of temporary barriers and netting allowing debris and contaminated water into occupied spaces
controls: Obtain engineer-certified design for temporary barriers and netting showing load capacity, fixings, and wind resistance before installation.
Install netting and sheeting with certified fixings to balcony structure — use mechanical anchors, not adhesive, spaced per design.
Brace temporary barriers at base with adjustable props or diagonal bracing to prevent sideways or outward movement.
Check netting for tears, holes, or loose edges before and after each work shift — repair or replace immediately.
Barricade interior edges of temporary barriers with high-visibility tape and warning signs to prevent trip hazards.
Establish resident communication schedule — confirm water and power isolation dates 48 hours before shutdown.
Isolate water and power supplies using lockable isolation switches tagged with warning notices before work affects those services.
Monitor exterior wind speed during works — stop work if sustained wind exceeds 40 km/h or gusts exceed 60 km/h.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install netting until: engineer design certificate with load calculations and fixing details is signed and on site.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not shut water or power until: residents have been notified in writing 48 hours before, and isolation is supervised by a competent person.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: netting or barriers show visible sagging, bulging, or separation from fixings.
🛑 STOP WORK if: sustained wind speed exceeds 40 km/h or gusts exceed 60 km/h during work.
🛑 STOP WORK if: debris accumulates on barriers faster than it can be cleared, increasing load risk.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licensed scaffolder before any temporary structure work starts.
Obtain signed working at heights permit before each elevated task on balconies or at height.
Complete handover certificate for temporary barriers before any worker enters or passes below protected areas.
Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and relevant scaffold or heights competency before starting.
Establish daily site inspection log — document netting condition, fixings, debris load, wind conditions, and any defects.
Brief residents on work schedule, water and power isolation times, and access restrictions before work begins.
Obtain SDS for netting membrane product and brief workers on hazards before use.

monitoring.critical_control: Check netting and barrier fixings for tears, separation, or loose edges before and after each shift.
monitoring.frequency: before work starts each day, after completion each day, and continuous during works
monitoring.evidence: Daily site inspection log entries, photographs of barrier condition, defect register if repairs needed.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Isolate and protect occupied spaces
responsibility.WKR: Perform Isolate and protect occupied spaces per SWMS

tasks.scope: Apply screed to membrane at specified fall and finish level. Set tile bed and install tiles. Point and grout. HOLD: Leo and Associates inspection before grouting completion.
hazards: Manual handling injury from screed application — repetitive low-back strain from troweling and smoothing screed
Slip hazard on wet screed surface during tiling and setting operations
Cuts and puncture wounds from tile edges, setting tools, and sharp grout mixers
Chemical irritation or dermatitis from grout, cement, and tile adhesive products
Heat stress during hot weather curing period in confined balcony conditions
tasks.dominant_hazard: Manual handling injury from screed application and tiling over extended balcony length
controls: Apply screed in sections not exceeding 2 m² to control repetitive troweling duration and reduce low-back strain.
Use knee pads and work from kneeling position during tiling and screed smoothing to reduce sustained low-back flexion.
Rotate workers between screed application and tile setting every 2 hours to limit cumulative manual handling exposure.
Keep screed surface dry between tiling operations — mop excess water immediately to prevent slip hazard.
Wear cut-resistant gloves (Level 5 protection) when handling tile edges and mixing tools.
Review SDS for tile adhesive and grout before work starts — confirm ventilation is adequate for occupied space.
Protect skin from cement and grout contact — wear hi-viz shirt or vest
Stop work if ambient temperature exceeds 32 °C — implement extended breaks and increase water access in balcony area.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to grouting until: Leo and Associates inspection completed and signed off on tile bed set, fall, and level compliance.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker reports acute low-back pain, stiffness, or radiating pain during or immediately after screed application.
🛑 STOP WORK if: screed surface becomes saturated or slippery and cannot be dried within 10 minutes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupants report respiratory irritation or headache from adhesive or grout fumes in adjacent spaces.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Confirm scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and posted on site before any worker accesses elevated work.
Verify working at heights permit is issued and current for all elevated tiling and screed operations.
Obtain SDS for tile adhesive, grout, and cement products and store on site in accessible location.
Establish water supply point on scaffold to allow immediate cleaning of tools, skin, and spillage during work.
Coordinate with building occupants — tell of work schedule and chemical odour risk; establish complaint line.
Record Leo and Associates inspection sign-off before grouting begins — retain copy on file.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Hard hat with chin strap (fall risk from balcony edge proximity)
Knee pads or kneeling mat (screed and tile setting position)
Long-sleeve cotton shirt (cement and grout irritant protection)
Respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) if grout dust or adhesive fumes detected indoors)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: before tile bed setting starts and after each water application
monitoring.evidence: Visual check of surface condition; supervisor sign-off on work checklist; note any slip incidents or near-misses in daily log.

responsibility.SUP: Verify fall protection, check module weights, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Wear fall harness, check lanyard attachment, report equipment damage

tasks.scope: Refit or install balustrade posts and rails, edge trim, and any removed fittings. make sure structural attachment to slab per original design or engineer direction.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Fall from height — balustrade removal exposes unguarded edge over 4m during reinstallation works
Dropped objects from balustrade components onto occupied areas below during handling and installation
Manual handling injury from heavy balustrade posts and rails — awkward positioning at height
Crush injury if balustrade frame or trim falls during handling or installation
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — unguarded balcony edge during balustrade reinstallation and structural attachment
controls: Obtain engineer's written approval for balustrade design, fixing method, and load capacity before any installation starts.
Confirm scaffold is erected, tagged, and certified with handover certificate before any worker accesses the edge.
Install temporary edge protection (guardrail or netting) on the unguarded edge immediately after balustrade removal — do not leave edge unguarded between removal and reinstallation.
Wear a fall arrest harness connected to a fixed anchor point whenever working within 2 m of the unguarded edge, before and during balustrade reinstallation.
Use a mechanical hoist or counterbalance to raise balustrade posts and rails to working height — no manual lifting above shoulder height.
Strap or net each balustrade component during handling to prevent dropped objects onto occupied areas below.
Check all balustrade attachment bolts and fasteners are tight and match engineer specification before signing off each section.
Brief all workers on the balustrade design, fixing sequence, and edge protection procedure at the start of each shift.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install balustrade posts until: temporary edge protection is fully installed and visually confirmed on unguarded edges.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not hand over completed balustrade section to occupants until: engineer inspection confirms all fixings match design and load test is passed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker is found working at the edge without a harness connected to a certified anchor point.
🛑 STOP WORK if: a balustrade component shows signs of structural damage, corrosion, or stress cracking during installation.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any fastener, bolt, or weld is found loose or non-compliant with engineer specification during final check.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain engineer's written approval for balustrade design before purchase or installation.

Conduct a pre-start toolbox talk covering balustrade sequence, edge protection, harness anchors, and dropped-object zones.
Record all balustrade fixings, bolt torque settings, and load test results in a commissioning logbook.
tell site occupants of balustrade reinstatement schedule and restricted access zones before work starts.

Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels

monitoring.critical_control: Verify fall arrest harness is connected to certified anchor before worker moves within 2 m of unguarded edge.
monitoring.frequency: continuous during elevated work, check-in every 15 minutes
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of harness clip attachment; supervisor sign-off on daily log; photographic record of temporary edge protection in place

tasks.task: Reinstate occupied spaces and temporary protection removal
tasks.scope: Remove netting, sheeting, and temporary barriers. Clean balconies and accessible interior areas of dust and debris. Restore resident access and tell stakeholders of completion.
hazards: Uncontrolled release of dust and debris into occupied spaces during netting and barrier removal
Collapse of temporary barriers during removal leading to falling debris or netting
Trip hazard from temporary fixings, residual netting, and cleaning debris during interior reinstatement
Contaminated dust inhalation by residents during concurrent cleaning and barrier removal
tasks.dominant_hazard: Uncontrolled release of dust and contaminated debris into occupied spaces during protection removal
controls: Wet down netting and sheeting with water spray before removal to suppress dust release into occupied spaces.
Remove netting and sheeting in sections, starting from top, onto drop sheets or containment to prevent debris scatter.
Vacuum all horizontal surfaces with HEPA-filtered vacuum before manual wiping to capture settled dust.
Wipe balconies and accessible interior areas with damp cloths — do not dry sweep or brush.
Bag all removed netting, sheeting, and cleaning debris immediately in sealed heavy-duty bags.
Check temporary fixings, bolts, and brackets are fully removed and surfaces cleared before resident access.
tell residents 24 hours before removal work and confirm occupancy status before starting each day.
Conduct final walkthrough with PM to confirm all barriers removed, surfaces clean, and no trip hazards remain.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove netting or sheeting until: water suppression system is operational and occupants have been notified and relocated from immediate work zones
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression fails during netting removal or dust becomes visible in occupied spaces
🛑 STOP WORK if: residents are present in the immediate work area during barrier or netting removal
admin: Obtain occupancy notification log signed by residents or site manager before work start each day.
Brief all workers on location of occupied spaces and no-entry zones before starting.
Record netting and barrier removal completion with site photo evidence.
Obtain PM sign-off on final reinstatement walkthrough before telling stakeholders of completion.
ppe: Respiratory protection (P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum) during removal and dry-wiping tasks if dust is visible.
Disposable coveralls during netting removal and damp wiping to prevent clothing contamination.

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: continuous during removal
monitoring.evidence: Water visible on netting surface; no visible dust clouds during removal; supervisor observation log

responsibility.WKR: Wear fall harness, check lanyard attachment, report equipment damage

tasks.scope: Walk balconies for defects, cracking, poor finish, or water ingress risk. Record and remedy. Leo and Associates final inspection and approval required before handover.
tasks.hrcw_category: cl.2 — Construction work at height — risk of fall >2m
hazards: Trip hazard from balcony surface irregularities, dust, and debris during inspection walk
Fall from height — balcony edge exposure during inspection and close examination of defects
Contact with damp concrete or grout residues creating slip hazard on balcony surface
Inhalation of dust if defect remediation requires grinding or surface preparation rework
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during close inspection of balcony edge and defects at height
controls: Walk balcony surface methodically in straight lines, stopping at each defect zone before close examination.
Clear balcony surface of dust, debris, and loose material with damp cloth or vacuum before inspection walk starts.
Wear non-slip footwear with ankle support on all balcony surfaces during inspection.
Position body with centre of gravity minimum 1 m back from balcony edge during visual defect assessment.
Use handheld inspection mirror or phone camera to examine defects within 0.5 m of edge without leaning.
Record defect location, type, and severity on site inspection sheet before remediation planning.
Brief all workers on occupied building protocols: no loud power tools before 8 am or after 5 pm on weekdays.
Isolate remediation work area with temporary hoarding if defect rework requires grinding, cutting, or dust generation.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start remediation work until: Leo and Associates has reviewed inspection report and approved defect repair scope in writing
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not use balcony for inspection until: scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and scaff tag is attached and visible
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker trips or loses balance during inspection walk — do not resume until surface hazard is identified and controlled
🛑 STOP WORK if: defect rework generates visible dust or airborne material without dust extraction or local ventilation active
